message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is behind Berlin (Central European Time).  
Because both regions observe daylight‑saving time, the offset varies through the year:

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Time Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|-----------------|
| Standard time (winter) | Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC−08:00) | Central European Time (CET, UTC+01:00) | **+9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| Daylight‑saving time (summer) | Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC−07:00) | Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+02:00) | **+8 hours** (Berlin is 8 h ahead) |

**Typical DST schedule**

* **Los Angeles:** Starts second Sunday in March (clocks forward one hour), ends first Sunday in November (clocks back one hour).
* **Berlin:** Starts last Sunday in March (clocks forward one hour), ends last Sunday in October (clocks back one hour).

Because the start/end dates differ by a week, there are brief periods (a few days each year) when the offset is 7 or 10 hours instead of the usual 8 or 9. If you need the exact difference for a specific date, let me know!
